newsitem.title: CANADA: TCPL, Northern States eyeing pipeline.
newsitem.headline: TCPL, Northern States eyeing pipeline.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd confirmed on Wednesday it was in preliminary discussions with Northern States Power Co of Minneapolis on possibly building a natural gas pipeline valued as high as US$900 million.
"It's an extremely preliminary time in the discussions," TransCanada spokesman David Annesley said. "We don't announce anything at this stage."

He said the companies filed a non-binding letter of intent with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The move alerted shareholders the firms were discussing a 1 billion-1.2 billion cubic feet per day pipeline that would supply customers in North Dakota, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Illinois with Canadian gas.

The line would extend from where NSP unit Viking Gas Transmission interconnects with TCPL's system near the Canada-U.S. border near Noyes, Minnesota. TCPL would also take a 50-percent stake in Viking if the proposal went ahead.
Annesley said the proposal, which would only proceed if market conditions warrant, would likely be valued between US$800 million and US$900 million.
He said a proposed in-service date of November 2000 was not finalized.
